title: Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17, August 2026 data) — 9:15 a.m. ET on triple-witching Friday, the first ordinary G.17 date the Atlanta Fed has scheduled no nowcast vintage for
source: FED: two independent federalreserve.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 — the Board's G.17 announcements feed (feeds/g17.html, HTTP 200, 614,006 bytes) states verbatim "In 2026, the G.17 release on Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization will be published at 9:15 a.m. on January 16, February 18, March 16, April 16, May 15, June 15, July 17, August 18, September 18, October 16, November 17, and December 16", and the Board's own release-date table (releases/g17/release_dates.htm, HTTP 200, 117,098 bytes, footer "Last Update: August 18, 2026") carries the row "September 2026 | 18-September-2026" in a maintained table that runs to December 2027 and still records "October 2025 NA" / "November 2025 NA" from the funding lapse. The same feed publishes the 2027 schedule too, so this date sits inside a two-year forward calendar rather than at its edge. PROMOTED from the estimate the nahb-hmi-2026-10-19 sweep filed, which said in its own notes that it could not self-confirm an in-sweep discovery and that the precedent for promotion was one step away — this is that session, reading the same two Federal Reserve primaries directly. The Board's verb is "will be published", not the "anticipated" that keeps the Census siblings at estimate. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, after reading the single proposal that existed for this id (proposals/industrial-production-2026-09-18.from-nahb-hmi-2026-10-19.json, now shadowed and inert). The proposal's facts all survive; its scope caveat — that it was filed from 31 days away, outside the 5-day adjacency radius — is moot now that the id has its own canonical entry. The reference month is AUGUST 2026, month 2 of the Q3-2026 quarter GDPNow has been nowcasting since 2026-07-30. Impact LOW and symbols empty on measured grounds. TWO structural facts separate this edition from its already-researched November and December siblings. (1) THE ATLANTA FED SCHEDULES NO GDPNOW VINTAGE ON 2026-09-18. Across the model's whole archive, 140 of the 142 G.17 release dates in span carried a same-day vintage (98.6%), and the only two that did not — 2019-02-15 and 2025-12-23 — were both produced by funding lapses; the Atlanta Fed's own PostedUpdates sheet schedules a 2026 vintage on just 5 of the Board's 12 G.17 dates, and 09-18 is one of the seven that get none (nearest vintages 09-17 housing starts and 09-25 M3-1). So this print would be the first no-vintage G.17 date in the archive produced by ordinary scheduling rather than a shutdown, and the nowcast channel the siblings measured is not merely quiet here, it is absent on the day. (2) 2026-09-18 IS QUARTERLY TRIPLE WITCHING (opex-2026-09-18, tracked, high) and BoJ decision day (boj-decision-2026-09-18, tracked, medium, decided overnight ET). The one window a 09:15 release could own is the overnight gap, and it is already spoken for: on SPY since 2014-05 (baseline n=3,106, gap 0.2822%) a quarterly witching gaps 0.4870% at p=0.0012, while a G.17 standing alone gaps 0.3088% at p=0.5440 and a September G.17 that is NOT a witching gaps 0.0869% at p=0.0812 — narrower than an ordinary open. Both of the two September G.17s that fell on a witching (2017-09-15, 2023-09-15) gapped in the expiration's class, at 0.560% and 0.715%. No house playbook is macro-keyed (grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-run 2026-09-06, 0 hits) and no instrument attaches. The live variable remains the 2026 ANNUAL REVISION — new 2022 base year, 2023 Census manufacturing benchmark, capacity through Q4-2025 — announced 2026-05-15 for "the autumn of 2026" and still undated on both the feed and the current release page as of today. It is very unlikely to touch this print: no annual revision in the feed's archive has ever been published on a monthly G.17 date (0 of 12; every one was a standalone noon release), and the shortest dated-notice-to-publication lead on record is 11 days (2023) against 12 days remaining today. Date confirmed; nothing here licenses an entry.
